insights: The JaCoCo coverage bundle for integration-tests measures almost nothing real: every main class it sees is a generated quarkus-grpc stub, so the bundle reports a near-zero branch ratio (0.13 observed) that no hand-written test can raise. The check is kept meaningful by a class-name-prefix-scoped coverage exclusion for the generated stubs; do not chase this ratio with new tests.

purpose_reasoning: Failsafe IT sources plus Docker infrastructure behind the integration-tests and jfr profiles; skipPublishing=true; src/main holds only the GrpcEchoService test upstream (quarkus-grpc), no product code
responsibility: Integration test coordinator: builds the native api-sheriff container image and, via the integration-tests profile, orchestrates the Docker Compose stack its Failsafe IT suites run against with REST Assured and Awaitility. The IT families cover container health, metrics and image metadata; config load and fail-closed refusal; bearer validation and the inbound pipeline guards (host smuggling, GET-with-body, body limits, error contract, security-profile modes, graceful shutdown); the server-session and sealed-cookie BFF flows (login, refresh, logout, CSRF, userinfo); the TLS edge (mTLS, SNI passthrough, management plain-HTTP opt-out, upstream hostname verification); gRPC, WebSocket and asset relays. Surefire *WiringTest classes pin the compose and descriptor wiring those ITs rely on; the separate jfr profile builds api-sheriff:jfr and runs ImageMetadataJfrIT.

tips: Local 'verify -Ppre-commit' does NOT run the Docker integration-tests profile (-Pintegration-tests). Integration-affecting changes (IT script assertions, mounted-config permissions/paths, Dockerfile/compose edits) pass the local pre-commit gate but are only validated in CI. Run 'verify -Pintegration-tests -pl integration-tests -am' locally before pushing any integration-affecting change.
